newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ downgrades 1997 profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ downgrades 1997 profit forecast.

text.p: The Czech power utility CEZ a.s. said on Friday that low demand for electricity and creation of reserves would cause 1997 net profit, according to Czech accounting standards (CAS), to fall about two billion crowns below the company's original forecast of 6.1 billion.

"The 1997 budget... (written) at the end of 1996, expects profit after tax of CZK 6.1 billion. These expectations were based on the increasing demand for electricity. Now we expect a decrease of demand for electricity by 1 percent," the company said in a statement.

"(The lower expected demand) in connection with expected provisions for unrealised losses in exchange rates will lead to the decrease of net profit appoximately by two billion crowns in comparison with the annual budget."
The company did not release a forecast for 1997 profit under international accounting standards (IAS).

Earlier CEZ said that interim IAS after-tax profit fell to 3.53 billion crowns compared with 5.95 billion for the six-month period last year as demand for electricity fell by 2.4 percent, year-on-year.

Earnings per common share fell to 65.65 crowns for the period from 110.70. Net operating profit fell to 7.53 billion crowns from 9.72 billion, as operating revenues fell to 28.17 billion crowns from 28.51 billion while operating expenses rose to 20.64 billion crowns from 18.79 billion.
